001: Ivan, have you already done your history homework?
Not yet, I just started reading the chapter. Have you already finished everything?
Almost, I just need to write the conclusion. The material is pretty difficult.
Really? Then maybe we can work on it together at the library tomorrow?
Sure. Let's meet after the second class, if you can make it.
Deal. I'll come as soon as I'm free.
002: Dmitry, do you know where we're supposed to submit the philosophy essay?
Usually we turn it in at the department office, but this time they said to send it by email.
By Friday, by six in the evening.
Thanks, I was afraid I was already late.
No problem. You still have a couple of days to check everything.
003: Olga, has the teacher already graded our tests?
Yes, he returned them at the last class. Your paper is in his office.
Did he say when we can pick them up?
He said we can come by on Wednesday after the lecture.
Great, I'll stop by. And how did you do?
I got a B, but he said I can retake it if I fix the mistakes.
004: Sergey, have you already sent your essay for review?
Yes, I sent it yesterday evening. You haven't yet?
No, I just can't finish the last paragraph.
I can't phrase the conclusion so that it sounds convincing.
Try starting with the main point, and then add some examples. It should work out.
005: Maria, do you remember what format we need to submit the lab report in?
They told us to bring a printed copy and attach the file on a flash drive.
And is the title page really required?
Yes, without it they won't accept the work. Last time I lost points because of that.
Got it, thanks for the heads-up.
No problem. If you need, I can send you an example of the formatting.
006: Alexey, have you already submitted your term paper for review?
No, I decided to read through the introduction one more time. There are a couple of weak spots.
By the end of the month, but I want to turn it in early so I have time to fix any comments.
That's the right approach. Last semester I waited until the last day and really regretted it.
Yeah, I don't want to repeat your mistake. Better to get everything done ahead of time.
007: Elena, do you know if we can submit the homework after class?
Usually you can, but it's better to let the teacher know in advance.
Won't he get upset about it being late?
I don't think so, if you explain the reason. The main thing is not to stay silent.
Okay, I'll write him an email tonight.
Yes, that's the right thing to do. He appreciates it when students let him know ahead of time.
008: Ivan, have you seen where they put our literature essays?
They're on the class monitor's desk. I saw them this morning.
Can we already take ours back, or is it too early?
I think so. The teacher said we can pick them up after class.
Great, I'll grab mine and look at the comments.
Just don't forget to return the grade sheet if there is one.
009: Olga, have you already done the English text translation?
Yes, I finished yesterday. Are you still working on it?
Yeah, I just have the last paragraph left. There are a lot of unfamiliar words.
If you want, I can give you my little dictionary.
That would be great, thanks. I'll return it tomorrow.
Okay, just don't lose it. I need it myself to prepare for the exam.
010: Dmitry, do you know if the teacher has already posted the grades for the essays?
Yes, he said the grades will appear in the online gradebook by the evening.
Have you already found out yours?
Yeah, I got a B. It's a bit disappointing, but I know what I need to fix.
That's still a good result. I'm worried I didn't develop the topic enough.
Don't worry ahead of time. Wait until the evening and then decide what to do.
